html:
Geawegal is the name recorded for an Aboriginal Australian people of the upper Hunter Valley in eastern New South Wales, north of Sydney.

The linguist Jim Wafer of Newcastle University has questioned this identification and reconstructed a different original name. Their neighbours were the Wonnarua of the central valley, the Darkinjung to the south and the Birrbay and Worimi toward the coast. Settlers took grants along the Hunter from the 1820s, and the valley became farming, horse breeding and later coal country.
sum: Geawegal is the name recorded for an Aboriginal Australian people of the upper Hunter Valley in eastern New South Wales, north of Sydney.
